key_insight: V-PaSS improves predictions for unfamiliar perovskite solar cells by representing alloy physics and device architecture rather than treating materials as arbitrary labels.
engineering_relevance: The approach could help screen new absorber alloys and transport-layer combinations before committing to device fabrication.
method: Interpolate relaxed crystal graphs of 23 pure ABX₃ endpoints using Vegard’s law with learned bandgap bowing.
Encode layer order, cell polarity, and interfacial band offsets.
Represent chemical descriptions with a scientific language model.
evidence_signal: On tests restricted to unseen laboratories, untuned V-PaSS achieved 2.861% MAE versus 3.017% for a gradient-boosted baseline; reported error reductions reached 15.7–19.0% on unseen absorber alloys.
watch_item: Alloy interpolation relies on physical-continuity assumptions, so accuracy for compositions outside the represented solid-solution behavior requires validation.
paper_title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells
